e.meaning: something handed down from the past
e.etymology: A respelling of Legacy, the English word for what a person leaves to those who come after. Legacy joined Legend and Destiny as an American given name in recent decades.
A modern American name that adds the -lee ending to Knox, a Scottish surname from Gaelic cnoc, hill.
A recent variation on Kehlani with a D- beginning, in the style of Hawaiian names ending in -lani.
Known from the actress Marsai Martin of Black-ish, whose fame carried the name onto the charts. Its origin is not documented.
namesakes: Marsai Martin (actress in Black-ish and Little)

e.etymology: A medieval name found in England and France, probably from Latin amicus, friend. It has returned through Amicia de Rune, heroine of the video game A Plague Tale.
A spelling of Marcy, the pet form of Marcia, the feminine of the Roman name Marcius, which goes back to Mars, the god of war.
The Provençal form of Marguerite, from Greek margarites, pearl. It spread through France after Frédéric Mistral's 1859 poem Mirèio, which includes a song to Magali.
From the Tamil word kavin, beauty, grace or comeliness.
A respelling of Mekhi, an African American coinage made familiar by the actor Mekhi Phifer in the late 1990s and 2000s.
In Welsh a pet form of Siân, the Welsh Jane, from Hebrew for God is gracious. In the United States it is mostly said in three syllables and used as a modern name.

e.meaning: little poet (Irish); or darling, fair (Welsh Tegan)
e.etymology: A respelling of Teagan. For boys Teagan is from an Irish surname based on a pet form of Tadhg, poet; for girls it is a variant of Tegan, from Welsh tegan, pet or darling.
From Hebrew peninah, pearl. In the First Book of Samuel, Peninnah is the wife of Elkanah and the rival of Hannah.
The feminine of Arabic Habib, beloved or darling, from hubb, love.
A spelling of Iliana or Ilyana. Iliana is a form of Helen used in Spanish, and Ilyana is a Russian feminine of Ilya, Elijah. Illyana Rasputin is the X-Men character Magik.
From Sanskrit shreyan, a form of shreyas, better or more excellent, a word used in the Bhagavad Gita for the higher good.
From Arabic mubarak, blessed, from the root of baraka, blessing. The same word appears in the greeting Eid Mubarak, a blessed festival.

assoc.t: Hosni Mubarak, president of Egypt until 2011
Eid Mubarak, the greeting for Muslim festivals

e.etymology: Has several possible sources, among them the Hebrew name Niva, from niv, speech or expression.
A modern American coinage in the family of Jaylon and Daylon, with the Zay- of Zayden.

e.meaning: olive tree (by tradition); possibly ancestor's heir
e.etymology: A respelling of Oliver, from Old French Olivier. The name was long linked to Latin oliva, olive, but it probably started as a Germanic or Norse name such as Olaf, ancestor's heir.
The English word, from Old English bletsian, to consecrate. It is a recent name of gratitude, alongside Blessing and Miracle.
A South Asian spelling of Rayyan, from Arabic rayyan, well-watered or luxuriant. In Islamic tradition Ar-Rayyan is the gate of paradise reserved for those who fast.
A spelling of Zain or Zayn, from Arabic zayn, beauty, grace or adornment.
Several names meet here: Hebrew Ro'i, my shepherd, as in Psalm 23; a spelling of Roy that matches French roi, king; and the Galician short form of Rodrigo, famous ruler.
From the ancient Greek name Theon, built on theos, god. Theon of Alexandria was a 4th-century mathematician and the father of Hypatia.

assoc.t: Theon Greyjoy in Game of Thrones

e.etymology: A Latin American spelling of Justin that writes the English pronunciation in Spanish letters. Justin is from Latin Justinus, from justus, just.
The Spanish, Portuguese and Italian name of the river Nile, from Latin Nilus. It is given in honor of saints called Nilus, among them Saint Nilus of Sinai.

e.meaning: love with jasmine, pear or village, depending on the kanji
e.etymology: A Japanese girls' name that usually opens with ai, love, followed by ri written as jasmine, pear, village or reason. A separate Finnish and Estonian Airi was coined around 1900.

e.meaning: a banded gemstone, best known in black
e.etymology: A spelling of Onyx that matches ónix, the Spanish word for the gemstone. The word comes from Greek onyx, claw or fingernail, after the pale bands in some stones.
A respelling of Emiliana, or an elaboration of Amelia with the -ana ending.
A clipped form of Emmanuel, from Hebrew for God is with us. It spread with the Puerto Rican rapper Anuel AA, born Emmanuel Gazmey Santiago.
namesakes: Anuel AA (Puerto Rican Latin trap star)

assoc.t: Anuel AA, Puerto Rican Latin trap star

e.etymology: A recent American coinage that joins the Zar- of Zara and Zariah to the -ielle ending of Arielle and Brielle.
An extended form of Saanvi, a modern Indian name often described as a name of the goddess Lakshmi, with the -ka ending.
